newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Mobutu says he is recovering from surgery.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu says he is recovering from surgery.

text.p: Zaire's veteran president, Mobutu Sese Seko, has told the nation that he is resting in Switzerland after a prostate operation and plans to return home in the near future.
Mobutu, speaking by telephone from Lausanne, told state television late on Friday, that he was no longer under medical supervision.
"I have been operated on. I am resting. I am not under medical supervision. I am at the hotel," he said. "It is no longer necessary to see the doctor."
Mobutu, who seized power in a 1965 coup, is due to contest a presidential election next year for the first time. In past elections, he has been unopposed.
He told the television in the telephone call, which was recorded earlier in the evening, that he would return to Zaire "soon" but gave no indication of the date.
Zaire's transition to democracy, launched by Mobutu in 1990 under strong internal and external pressure, has lagged well behind that of other states in the region.
According to the transitional constitution, which was extended again last July, multi-party presidential and parliamentary elections must be held by July 1997.
